content.user_title: Run Conversational QA and File GitHub Issues
content.value_statement: Bug reports often lack reproducible details and clear scope. This skill clarifies each report, applies project terminology, and files structured GitHub issues.
actual_capabilities: Asks up to three concise questions about expected behavior, actual behavior, reproduction steps, and consistency.
Explores the codebase in the background to learn domain language and intended feature behavior.
Determines whether a report needs one issue or several independently actionable issues.
Writes concise, user-focused issue bodies with mandatory reproduction steps.
Creates GitHub issues through `gh issue create` and returns their URLs.
Orders dependent issues and records blocking relationships for parallel work.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI and permission to create issues in the active repository.
Does not diagnose root causes or implement fixes.
Excludes file paths and line references from issue bodies by design.
Requires reproduction steps and may ask for more details when they are missing.

use_cases.title: Convert Test Reports
use_cases.description: Convert a tester's conversational bug report into a concise issue with expected behavior and reproduction steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Support Escalations
use_cases.description: Turn customer-reported symptoms into developer-ready GitHub issues using the project's domain language.

use_cases.title: Break Down Broad Defects
use_cases.description: Split broad defects into ordered, independently actionable issues with explicit blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Report a Clear Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a QA session. The settings page saves successfully, but my timezone resets after refresh.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the observed and expected behaviors are already clear.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an Intermittent Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Run QA for an intermittent checkout failure. Ask concise questions, then file one issue when reproduction details are sufficient.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when frequency or triggering conditions remain uncertain.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Project Terminology
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a durable issue for duplicated imported records after synchronization retries. Explore project terminology before writing the issue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the report should match established product language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dependency Breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess and file an ordered issue breakdown: validation fails, success feedback is missing, and redirect behavior is incorrect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when one report contains several separable failure modes.

output_examples.input: The profile form says it saved, but the display name returns after I reload.
output_examples.output: Issue filed: Profile display name reverts after refresh. The body includes observed behavior, expected behavior, numbered reproduction steps, and the GitHub issue URL.

output_examples.input: Checkout rejects valid addresses, shows no success message, and sometimes stays on the payment page.
output_examples.output: Three focused issues are filed in dependency order. Each includes its own expected behavior, reproduction steps, blockers, and GitHub issue URL.

best_practices: Provide concrete expected and actual outcomes with exact reproduction steps.
Confirm the active repository and issue destination before starting the session.
Share relevant conditions such as configuration, inputs, frequency, and environment.
anti_patterns: Do not use automatic filing for confidential reports that must not reach GitHub.
Do not combine unrelated symptoms into one broad issue.
Do not expect root-cause analysis or code fixes from this workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill write or change code?
faq.answer: No. It explores context only to improve issue wording and does not implement fixes.

faq.question: Does it create GitHub issues automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the authenticated `gh issue create` command after collecting sufficient details.

faq.question: Will it ask me to approve each issue?
faq.answer: No. The current workflow files issues without preflight review, so use it only when automatic filing is acceptable.

faq.question: Can it split one report into several issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It separates independent failure modes and records genuine blocking relationships.

faq.question: Why does it explore the codebase?
faq.answer: It learns product terminology, intended behavior, and user-facing boundaries for clearer issue descriptions.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need an authenticated GitHub CLI, an active repository, and permission to create issues.
